subject.title: Owner-signed responsibility gates for assistant memory, actions, skills, and evidence reuse

question: Should OpenClaw define a core owner-confirmed responsibility lifecycle for memory and reusable evidence, or should this stay as plugin/ClawHub experimentation until a narrower API gap is proven?
rationale: The request crosses persistent state, security policy, plugin SDK contracts, UI/audit semantics, and public config; automation cannot safely choose the trust model or API boundary.

options.title: Sponsor a core design RFC
options.body: Keep this issue as the umbrella for a maintainer-owned design that specifies lifecycle states, storage/retrieval semantics, UI/audit behavior, and plugin extension points before implementation.

options.title: Split into narrower issues
options.body: Close or demote this umbrella only after creating canonical smaller issues for memory review state, provenance filters, action approvals, and evidence reuse policy.

options.title: Route external responsibility models to plugins
options.body: Treat SCBKR/UMP-style responsibility chains as ClawHub/plugin experiments unless they prove a missing core API needed for safe integration.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a core design RFC
recommendation.body: Keep this issue as the umbrella for a maintainer-owned design that specifies lifecycle states, storage/retrieval semantics, UI/audit behavior, and plugin extension points before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent Koc is the strongest current-main routing signal for the relevant plugin/memory/security surfaces after the recent broad refactor and current-line ownership.
